quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA Specific Learning Disability domains, statutory exclusionary clauses, dyslexia/dysgraphia/dyscalculia processing profiles, and multilingual differentiation.
checklist: Map the student’s documented achievement deficits onto IDEA’s 8 Specific Learning Disability academic areas rather than relying on broad classroom impressions.
Verify that exclusionary factors (vision/hearing/motor loss, ID, ED, cultural/economic disadvantage, limited English proficiency, or inadequate instruction) are not the primary cause.
Examine underlying language, phonological, orthographic, working-memory, and executive-function processes alongside coexisting ADHD or academic anxiety.
formulas: IDEA SLD 8 achievement areas (34 CFR 300.309(a)(1)): Oral Expression, Listening Comprehension, Written Expression, Basic Reading Skill, Reading Fluency Skills, Reading Comprehension, Mathematics Calculation, and Mathematics Problem Solving.

IDEA SLD exclusionary clause and inadequate-instruction rule-out (34 CFR 300.309(a)(3) & (b)): SLD excludes learning problems primarily resulting from visual, hearing, or motor disabilities, ID, ED, cultural factors, environmental/economic disadvantage, or limited English proficiency; teams MUST also confirm the child received appropriate reading and math instruction from qualified personnel plus repeated achievement assessments.

Core SLD processing profiles: Dyslexia (neurobiological word-recognition/decoding/spelling deficit rooted in phonological processing and slow orthographic mapping despite intact listening comprehension); Dysgraphia (transcription, orthographic-motor handwriting, and spelling bottlenecks); Dyscalculia (number-sense, magnitude comparison, subitizing, and fact-retrieval deficits).

Multilingual learner differentiation (Cummins): Basic Interpersonal Communicative Skills (BICS, social language, ~1 to 3 years) develop far faster than Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency (CALP, ~5 to 7+ years); true SLD manifests in BOTH L1 and L2 when adequate native-language instruction occurred.
decisionRules: When a 4th-grade student shows strong oral vocabulary and listening comprehension yet reads slowly with frequent vowel and multisyllabic decoding errors → prioritize suspecting a phonological/word-level reading profile (dyslexia pattern) and delivering explicit phonics and orthographic mapping.

When a newcomer multilingual student fluent in conversational English struggles with 5th-grade science texts after 18 months in U.S. schools → prioritize evaluating CALP development, L1 literacy history, and English-learner instructional scaffolds before attributing gaps to SLD.

When a student missed 45 school days across two years and changed schools three times before showing math calculation gaps → prioritize verifying whether inadequate or interrupted instruction (34 CFR 300.309(b)) explains the deficit before certifying SLD.

When a student with SLD avoids reading aloud and shows sudden stomachaches before literacy block → prioritize addressing skill-driven academic anxiety with private practice, explicit scaffolds, and growth-focused feedback.
cautions: Never assume dyslexia is a visual letter-reversal problem cured by colored overlays or vision therapy; evidence confirms dyslexia is primarily a language-based phonological processing disorder.
Do not interpret strong conversational English (BICS) as proof that a multilingual student possesses full academic English (CALP) for standardized English-only testing.
Avoid confusing IDEA’s SLD category with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder alone; ADHD qualifies under Other Health Impairment (OHI) unless a co-occurring SLD is also documented.

quickReference.domainLabel: Planning and Managing the Learning Environment
quickReference.title: Accommodations, Executive Function, UDL & SETT Assistive Tech
quickReference.purpose: Anchors accommodation versus modification boundaries, executive-function classroom scaffolds, UDL environment design, and SETT assistive-technology selection for SLD.
checklist: Verify whether a support removes an access barrier without changing grade-level standards (accommodation) or alters content expectations (modification).
Pinpoint which executive-function bottleneck (task initiation, working memory, planning, time estimation, self-monitoring) drives incomplete work.
Match assistive technology tools through the SETT framework and pair every tool with explicit student training and daily classroom integration.
formulas: Four accommodation categories (preserve grade-level standards): Presentation (text-to-speech, audiobooks/NIMAS/Bookshare, highlighted text, reduced visual clutter), Response (speech-to-text, word prediction, scribe, graphic organizers, calculator on problem-solving items), Setting (quiet testing space, preferential seating, study carrel), and Timing/Scheduling (extended time, chunked breaks, subtest scheduling).

Accommodations vs Modifications rule: accommodations change HOW a student accesses or demonstrates mastery and preserve standard-diploma accountability; modifications alter WHAT standards or complexity are required and must be justified cautiously by the IEP team.

Executive-function and self-regulation environment supports: break multi-step projects into dated checkpoints, post visual models/rubrics, teach binder/digital-folder organization explicitly, embed retrieval-practice warmups, and use cognitive self-monitoring checklists.

SETT Assistive Technology match for SLD: Student strengths/needs + Environments + Tasks → Tools (TTS/Bookshare for decoding bypass in content classes, STT/word prediction for severe transcription/spelling bottlenecks, digital mind-mapping for essay planning, math equation editors/graph paper for spatial alignment).
decisionRules: When an 8th grader with dyslexia demonstrates grade-level science reasoning orally but reads at a 3rd-grade decoding level → prioritize text-to-speech/audiobooks during science (access accommodation) alongside separate explicit decoding intervention (remediation), rather than simplifying science concepts.

When a high schooler with dysgraphia produces rich oral arguments yet writes only three fragmented sentences in 30 minutes → prioritize speech-to-text, word prediction, and structured outline templates matched via SETT while teaching revision routines.

When a student with SLD and executive-function weaknesses forgets long-term essay deadlines until the night before → prioritize teaching backward-calendar chunking, mini-deadlines with quick teacher check-ins, and a self-monitoring checklist.

When a classroom teacher offers extended time on tests without teaching pacing or providing access accommodations to a slow decoder → prioritize matching the specific accommodation to the documented functional barrier rather than defaulting to generic extended time.
cautions: Never use assistive technology bypass tools (such as text-to-speech) as a replacement for explicit remedial decoding or spelling instruction in elementary and middle grades—students need BOTH remediation and content access.
Do not list vague IEP accommodations such as "extended time as needed" or "preferential seating"; specify exact conditions (such as 1.5x time or front row away from the hallway door).
Avoid lowering grade-level content via modifications when a well-matched presentation or response accommodation lets the student master the standard.

quickReference.title: Structured Literacy, SRSD Writing & CRA/Schema Mathematics
quickReference.purpose: Anchors Simple View of Reading, Structured Literacy, fluency/comprehension routines, SRSD writing instruction, and CRA/schema-based math interventions.
checklist: Diagnose whether reading comprehension breaks down in Word Recognition (decoding/fluency), Language Comprehension (vocabulary/syntax/background), or both.
Separate transcription bottlenecks (handwriting/spelling) from composition-planning deficits before selecting a writing intervention.
Sequence mathematics instruction from concrete manipulatives to visual models to abstract symbols while teaching explicit word-problem schemas.
formulas: Simple View of Reading & Scarborough’s Reading Rope: Reading Comprehension equals Decoding (Word Recognition: phonological awareness, phonics/orthographic mapping, sight recognition) times Language Comprehension (background knowledge, vocabulary, language structures, verbal reasoning, literacy knowledge); weakness in either factor constrains comprehension.

Structured Literacy principles (IDA): explicit, systematic, cumulative, and diagnostic instruction across phonology, phoneme-grapheme correspondences, 6 syllable types (closed, open, VCe, vowel team, r-controlled, consonant-le), morphology (prefixes/roots/suffixes), syntax, and semantics; pair with repeated reading with feedback for fluency and Reciprocal Teaching / CSR for comprehension.

Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD) for written expression: 6 stages (Develop background knowledge, Discuss, Model, Memorize, Support, Independent performance) paired with mnemonics such as POW+TREE (Pick idea, Organize notes, Write/say more; Topic, Reasons, Explain, Ending) and STOP+DARE for persuasive essays, plus explicit sentence combining.

Evidence-based math instruction for SLD: Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA) sequence, explicit worked examples with think-alouds, Schema-Based Instruction (SBI: Combine/Total, Change, Compare; Equal Groups, Multiplicative Comparison—never fragile "keyword" tricks), and brief timed/untimed cumulative fact-retrieval practice.
decisionRules: When a 3rd grader decodes CVC words accurately but misreads multisyllabic words like "unpredictable" → prioritize teaching syllable-division routines (6 syllable types) and morphological analysis (prefix-root-suffix) explicitly rather than guessing from pictures.

When a 5th grader decodes accurately at 98% accuracy yet reads laboriously at 62 WCPM with poor recall → prioritize repeated reading with corrective feedback, phrase-cued prosody modeling, and morphological/Tier 2 vocabulary building.

When a middle schooler with written-expression SLD writes disorganized, single-paragraph opinion essays → prioritize walking systematically through all 6 SRSD stages with POW+TREE, graphic organizers, and self-monitoring rubrics.

When a student with math SLD sees the word "more" in a compare problem ("Sam has 12, which is 4 more than Jo") and erroneously adds 12 + 4 → prioritize replacing keyword rules with Schema-Based Instruction diagrams that model underlying quantitative relationships.
cautions: Never rely on three-cueing (guessing words from pictures or sentence context) for students with reading SLD; anchor word reading in phoneme-grapheme decoding and orthographic mapping.
Do not teach word-problem "keyword lists" (such as "altogether always means add"), which systematically break down on multi-step and inconsistent-language math problems.
Avoid moving directly to abstract math algorithms before a student demonstrates conceptual understanding at the concrete and representational stages.

quickReference.title: SLD Identification Models, Required Observation & Placement
quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA SLD evaluation statutes, MTSS/RTI versus PSW identification criteria, mandatory classroom observation, and LRE service-delivery placement rules.
checklist: Confirm that the multidisciplinary evaluation team includes the child’s regular teacher and at least one professional qualified to conduct individual diagnostic examinations.
Verify completion of a systematic academic classroom observation in the area of difficulty prior to the SLD eligibility determination.
Document inadequate achievement relative to age/grade standards AND inadequate response to scientific, research-based instruction (or state-approved PSW pattern).
formulas: IDEA SLD identification policy (34 CFR 300.307): states MUST NOT require the use of a severe discrepancy between intellectual ability and achievement, MUST permit a process based on the child’s response to scientific, research-based intervention (RTI/MTSS), and MAY permit other alternative research-based procedures (such as Patterns of Strengths and Weaknesses, PSW).

Mandatory SLD team composition and observation (34 CFR 300.308 & 300.310): evaluation group includes parents, regular education teacher, and a diagnostic specialist (such as school psychologist, SLP, or remedial reading teacher); at least one team member must observe academic performance in the regular classroom (or age-appropriate environment for out-of-school youth) and document written findings.

Required written SLD documentation (34 CFR 300.311): written eligibility report signed by each team member certifying agreement (or submitting a separate dissenting statement), explicitly addressing instructional adequacy, repeated progress data, classroom observation, medical findings, and exclusionary rule-outs.

LRE service-delivery continuum for SLD: prioritize general-education access with co-teaching or push-in consultation first, stepping to targeted resource pull-out for intensive structured literacy or math remediation only to the extent required for FAPE.
decisionRules: When an evaluation team attempts to disqualify a 2nd grader with severe reading failure solely because IQ-achievement discrepancy is 12 points instead of 15 → prioritize citing 34 CFR 300.307 (states cannot require severe discrepancy) and examining MTSS intervention response and achievement data.

When an SLD eligibility file contains IQ and achievement test scores but lacks classroom observation notes → prioritize completing and documenting a structured academic observation in the general-education setting (34 CFR 300.310) before finalizing eligibility.

When a team member disagrees with the group’s SLD eligibility conclusion during the meeting → prioritize documenting the member’s written dissenting statement per 34 CFR 300.311(b) rather than pressuring unanimous signatures.

When a student with SLD makes steady progress in general-education social studies and science with accommodations but needs intensive 45-minute daily structured literacy → prioritize a hybrid LRE schedule (inclusive content classes plus targeted resource reading block) rather than full-day pull-out.
cautions: Never use the "wait-to-fail" severe discrepancy model as an exclusive gatekeeper that withholds early reading intervention from primary-grade learners.
Do not accept Tier 3 MTSS progress data as valid SLD evidence unless intervention fidelity and student attendance were verified.
Avoid placing a student with SLD into a self-contained classroom purely because general-education co-teaching staffing is inconvenient.

quickReference.title: IDEA vs 504/ADA College Transition, Equity & Collaboration
quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA-to-postsecondary ADA/504 legal shifts, disproportionate identification safeguards, CEC ethical advocacy, and general-education/specialist partnerships.
checklist: Prepare high school students with SLD and their families early for the statutory shift from K-12 IDEA entitlement to college/workplace ADA/Section 504 self-disclosure.
Examine referral, evaluation, and placement data for racial, linguistic, or socioeconomic disproportionality before confirming SLD classifications.
Coordinate weekly instructional alignment across general educators, reading specialists, SLPs, families, and supervised paraprofessionals.
formulas: K-12 IDEA vs Postsecondary Section 504/ADA shift: K-12 districts have Child Find, fund evaluations, deliver FAPE/SDI via an IEP, and may modify curriculum; colleges and employers under ADA/504 require the STUDENT to self-disclose, submit current documentation (supported by the high school Summary of Performance), and receive reasonable accommodations without lowering essential course standards.

IDEA disproportionality safeguards (34 CFR 300.646): states monitor Significant Disproportionality by race/ethnicity across identification, placement, and discipline; districts flagged must reserve 15% of IDEA Part B funds for Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services (CCEIS) and review biased policies.

Summary of Performance (SOP, 34 CFR 300.305(e)(3)): mandatory upon graduation with a regular diploma or exceeding age eligibility; summarizes academic achievement, functional performance, and concrete accommodation recommendations to bridge postsecondary disability-services registration.

Interprofessional collaboration and evidence ethics: co-plan grade-level scaffolds with general educators, integrate SLP phonological/language goals with literacy intervention, reject pseudoscientific SLD cures (such as unproven visual-tracking or brain-gym fads), and protect FERPA confidentiality.
decisionRules: When a graduating senior with SLD assumes their IEP automatically transfers to state university classes → prioritize coaching the student on self-advocacy, disability-office intake, ADA/504 reasonable accommodations, and carrying their updated Summary of Performance.

When a parent asks the special educator to implement a commercial colored-lens or balance-board "dyslexia cure" instead of structured literacy → prioritize sharing peer-reviewed evidence respectfully while maintaining empirically validated structured literacy instruction.

When a school’s annual equity audit shows multilingual learners are over-identified as SLD in 4th grade → prioritize auditing Tier 1 literacy/ESL instruction, native-language evaluation practices, and MTSS fidelity before evaluating more students.

When a general-education math teacher and special educator disagree over grading a student’s accommodated test → prioritize clarifying IEP accommodations versus modifications together and ensuring accommodated grade-level work is graded on the standard scale without penalty.
cautions: Never penalize a student’s grade or mark transcripts with an asterisk solely because the student used an IEP-documented accommodation.
Do not wait until senior year May to teach a student with SLD how to explain their learning profile and request accommodations independently.
Avoid implementing untested commercial interventions that displace evidence-based reading, writing, or math instruction.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Ignoring SLD Exclusionary Criteria and Mistaking Lack of Instruction or ELL Status for SLD
misconceptionFamilies.description: Qualifying a student for Specific Learning Disability (SLD) without ruling out IDEA exclusionary factors—lack of appropriate instruction in reading or math, limited English proficiency, vision/hearing/motor disabilities, intellectual disability, emotional disturbance, or cultural/environmental/economic disadvantage—or falsely insisting an IQ-achievement discrepancy is federally mandatory.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Audit every SLD referral against both IDEA statutory guardrails: document appropriate core instruction and rule out all exclusionary factors as the primary cause (comparing emergent bilinguals against true language peers and native-language performance), and remember states must permit RTI or alternative research-based processes and may never mandate an IQ-achievement discrepancy.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Using RTI to Delay Parent-Requested Evaluations or Judging Nonresponse Without Fidelity Data
misconceptionFamilies.description: Telling families that a student must finish additional weeks of Tier 2 or Tier 3 Response to Intervention (RTI) before an IDEA initial evaluation can start, or declaring a student an "instructional nonresponder" when Tier 1 and Tier 2 interventions lacked documented implementation fidelity, dosage, and evidence-based alignment.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Follow OSEP Memo 11-07 strictly: RTI can never delay or deny a parent-requested IDEA initial evaluation (run RTI concurrently while evaluating or issue PWN if refusing), and verify Tier 1/Tier 2 fidelity checklists, attendance, and dosage before interpreting weak growth as intrinsic SLD.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Skipping the Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA) Progression in Math Remediation
misconceptionFamilies.description: Jumping straight into abstract symbolic algorithms, keyword tricks ("more means add"), or untaught timed fact sheets for students with math learning disabilities (dyscalculia) instead of explicitly bridging Concrete manipulatives, Representational drawings, and Abstract symbols alongside Schema-Based Instruction (SBI).
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Teach foundational number sense, fractions, and algebraic operations through explicit Concrete → Representational → Abstract (CRA) modeling with simultaneous math-language fade-in, and replace fragile keyword lists with Schema-Based Instruction that teaches underlying word-problem structures.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Correcting Surface Mechanics Instead of Explicit SRSD Writing and Executive Strategy Instruction
misconceptionFamilies.description: Responding to written-expression LD and dysgraphia with red-pen spelling corrections, unguided essay prompts, or isolated grammar drills rather than teaching Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD), cognitive mnemonics, and assistive technology such as speech-to-text or word prediction.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Implement the six recursive SRSD stages (develop background knowledge, discuss it, model it with think-alouds, memorize it, support it, independent performance) using genre mnemonics (such as POW+TREE) paired with transcription scaffolds and explicit self-regulation.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Making Instructional Changes Without CBM Trendlines and Data-Based Decision Rules
misconceptionFamilies.description: Judging IEP reading, writing, or math responsiveness from subjective teacher impressions, quarterly report-card grades, or one erratic quiz score instead of frequent Curriculum-Based Measurement (CBM) probes graphed against an aimline with clear decision rules.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Graph brief, standardized CBM probes weekly or biweekly against a baseline-to-goal aimline, apply the 4-point decision rule (4 consecutive points below aimline → intensify or alter instruction with a phase-change line; 4 consecutive points above → raise the goal), and use diagnostic error analysis to choose the exact instructional change.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Treating Dyslexia as a Visual Reversal Problem or Replacing Remediation with Accommodations Alone
misconceptionFamilies.description: Misattributing dyslexia to seeing letters backward and prescribing colored overlays or eye exercises instead of explicit structured literacy targeting the phonological-orthographic core deficit, or giving secondary students audiobooks and extended time while abandoning direct decoding, morphology, and study-strategy instruction.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Target dyslexia as a neurobiological language-based deficit in phonological processing and rapid orthographic mapping using explicit, systematic, cumulative structured literacy (phonemic awareness, phonics, syllable types, morphology), while pairing secondary access accommodations (audiobooks/TTS) with ongoing skill remediation.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Ignoring SLD Exclusionary Criteria and Mistaking Lack of Instruction or ELL Status for SLD
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Apply IDEA SLD Exclusionary Rules and Separate Language Difference from Disability
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: An eligibility vignette describes a student who missed half the year due to mobility, attended a school without systematic core reading instruction, or recently arrived as an English learner—yet a distractor rushes to qualify the student for SLD based on low English test scores alone.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Have we verified adequate opportunity to learn and ruled out all IDEA SLD exclusionary causes (lack of instruction, limited English proficiency, sensory/motor/ID/ED, environmental disadvantage) as the primary driver?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Scan the referral profile for exclusionary red flags (frequent absences, disrupted schooling, weak Tier 1 core instruction, emerging English proficiency, uncorrected vision/hearing issues) and check whether any distractor claims IDEA mandates a severe IQ-achievement discrepancy.
stages.requiredOutput: Identify the specific exclusionary factor or discrepancy-model myth present in the vignette.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Anchor IDEA's SLD determination requirements: (1) inadequate achievement across one or more of the eight SLD domains (oral expression, listening comprehension, written expression, basic reading, reading fluency, reading comprehension, math calculation, math problem-solving), (2) documented appropriate instruction by qualified personnel plus repeated progress data, (3) ruling out exclusionary factors as the primary cause, and (4) states cannot require an IQ-achievement discrepancy and must allow RTI or pattern of strengths and weaknesses (PSW).
stages.requiredOutput: State how a team distinguishes an English learner with normal second-language acquisition from an English learner who genuinely has an SLD (persistent difficulty in BOTH L1 and L2 relative to true language peers despite strong instruction).

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Evaluate two third-grade referrals: Case A moved across four schools in two years, missed phonics instruction, and jumped two grade levels during six weeks of explicit tutoring; Case B received three years of quality bilingual instruction, struggles with phonemic segmentation in both Spanish and English, and shows flat growth relative to bilingual peers.
stages.requiredOutput: Rule Case A ineligible for SLD due to lack of appropriate instruction and rapid instructional response, while explaining why Case B's cross-linguistic evidence supports SLD eligibility.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5383 eligibility item where a district psychologist refuses to consider RTI progress data because the student's IQ and reading scores lack a 15-point discrepancy.
stages.requiredOutput: Select the IDEA-compliant correction that federal law prohibits requiring a severe discrepancy and permits RTI-based SLD identification alongside comprehensive evaluation data.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Using RTI to Delay Parent-Requested Evaluations or Judging Nonresponse Without Fidelity Data
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Protect Parent Evaluation Rights Under OSEP Rules and Audit RTI Treatment Fidelity
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A parent submits a signed written request for an IDEA evaluation while their child is in Tier 2 RTI, and a distractor tells the parent they must wait 8 to 12 more weeks until Tier 3 concludes—or labels the student a nonresponder despite spotty intervention delivery.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Did the school respond immediately to the parent's evaluation request without using RTI as a gatekeeper, and did the team verify intervention fidelity, dosage, and alignment before calling the student a nonresponder?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Look for two high-frequency 5383 traps: using RTI stages to postpone an IDEA evaluation after a parent request, and interpreting flat Tier 2 scores without checking whether the intervention actually happened as designed.
stages.requiredOutput: Flag whether the stem violates OSEP's anti-delay mandate or skips RTI implementation-fidelity verification.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Separate the legal rule from the instructional audit: (1) Legally (OSEP Memo 11-07), when a parent requests an initial evaluation, the LEA must promptly seek consent and evaluate within IDEA timelines (continuing RTI concurrently) OR issue Prior Written Notice explaining why it refuses to evaluate; (2) Instructionally, valid RTI nonresponse requires verified core Tier 1 adequacy (at least 80% proficient), evidence-based Tier 2/3 protocol, trained provider, scheduled dosage/attendance, and fidelity observation checklists.
stages.requiredOutput: Write a two-part checklist: the exact legal step triggered by a parent evaluation request during RTI, and four fidelity indicators required before declaring Tier 2 nonresponse.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Analyze a fourth-grade RTI file showing zero reading growth over 8 weeks of Tier 2: logs reveal the group met only 9 of 24 planned sessions, group size swelled to 11 students, and the paraprofessional skipped the phonics decoding segment.
stages.requiredOutput: Explain why this data cannot validate SLD nonresponse and specify the immediate fidelity repairs (smaller group, consistent dosage, strict adherence to the validated decoding protocol) while noting that if the parent requests an evaluation, the school still cannot delay it.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Solve a fresh 5383 legal/RTI item where a principal instructs teachers to tell parents the district policy requires 18 weeks of documented MTSS before accepting any special education referral.
stages.requiredOutput: Identify the blanket 18-week policy as an IDEA violation and select immediate parent-referral processing with concurrent tiered supports.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Skipping the Concrete-Representational-Abstract (CRA) Progression in Math Remediation
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Scaffold Math LD Remediation Through Explicit CRA Bridges and Schema-Based Instruction
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A student with math LD (dyscalculia) reverses regrouping steps, misapplies fraction rules, or grabs numbers randomly in word problems—and distractors prescribe timed flashcard drills, keyword posters ("altogether = add"), or repetitive symbolic worksheets.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Have we explicitly linked Concrete manipulatives → Representational visual models → Abstract notation for the concept, and taught word-problem schemas rather than misleading keywords?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Inspect the student's math error pattern (place-value/regrouping breakdown, fraction magnitude confusion, or multi-step word-problem misinterpretation) and flag distractors that rely on rote abstract memorization or brittle keyword shortcuts.
stages.requiredOutput: Identify the conceptual math bottleneck and explain why the keyword or abstract-drill distractor fails students with math LD.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Map the explicit CRA sequence (Concrete: base-ten blocks, fraction tiles, algebra tiles with think-aloud → Representational: number lines, bar/tape diagrams, area drawings tied directly to the manipulatives → Abstract: numeric equations introduced alongside visuals before fading supports) plus Schema-Based Instruction (Additive: Total, Difference, Change; Multiplicative: Equal Groups, Comparison, Ratios/Proportions).
stages.requiredOutput: Outline a 3-stage CRA lesson sequence for subtracting across zeros or comparing unlike fractions, and show why "altogether" fails on a missing-part word problem compared to a Total schema.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: A fifth grader with dyscalculia writes 1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7 and adds every number whenever a word problem includes the word "more." Design the two-part remediation move.
stages.requiredOutput: Use fraction strips and number-line area models (CRA) to anchor common-unit meaning before symbolic common denominators, and teach the Difference/Comparison schema using a visual diagram instead of keyword matching.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5383 math-instruction vignette asking for the strongest evidence-based sequence to move a middle schooler with math LD from solving one-step equations with algebra tiles to symbolic notation.
stages.requiredOutput: Select explicit representational bridging (drawing tile diagrams paired directly with written algebraic steps and verbal think-alouds) before independent abstract practice.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Correcting Surface Mechanics Instead of Explicit SRSD Writing and Executive Strategy Instruction
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Teach Writing Explicitly via SRSD Stages, Genre Mnemonics, and Assistive Technology
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A student with dysgraphia or written-expression LD produces two disorganized sentences with numerous spelling errors, and distractors focus on copying corrected spelling words ten times or assigning extra journal prompts without planning scaffolds.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does the writing intervention explicitly teach planning, drafting, and self-regulation through all six SRSD stages while separating transcription barriers from compositional ideation via assistive technology?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Distinguish transcription bottlenecks (handwriting fluency, spelling mechanics) from executive/compositional bottlenecks (generating ideas, organizing genre elements, revising) and spot distractors that grade surface errors without teaching a cognitive strategy.
stages.requiredOutput: Diagnose whether the student's primary barrier is transcription, genre organization, or both, and flag any surface-correction-only distractor.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Sequence the six recursive Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD) stages (1. Develop Background Knowledge → 2. Discuss It → 3. Model It with explicit self-talk → 4. Memorize It → 5. Support It collaboratively with gradual release → 6. Independent Performance), pairing genre mnemonics (POW+TREE for persuasive writing, POW+WWW What=2 How=2 for narrative, STOP+DARE for secondary essays) with self-monitoring goal graphs and AT (speech-to-text, word prediction, graphic-organizer software).
stages.requiredOutput: Map each of the six SRSD stages to one concrete teacher action and specify when speech-to-text lowers cognitive load for a student with severe dysgraphia.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: A seventh grader with SLD in written expression speaks eloquently about climate solutions but freezes when asked to write a 3-paragraph persuasive argument and omits counterclaims. Build an SRSD + AT intervention.
stages.requiredOutput: Specify modeling POW+TREE (or STOP+DARE) with explicit self-statements, graphic-organizer planning, speech-to-text or word-prediction drafting to bypass transcription fatigue, and a self-scored checklist targeting all genre parts before editing conventions.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Evaluate a fresh 5383 writing item asking which stage of SRSD is missing when a teacher hands out a POW+TREE poster and expects students to write independently the very next day.
stages.requiredOutput: Identify the skipped teacher modeling (think-aloud with self-regulation), strategy memorization, and scaffolded collaborative support stages before independent performance.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Making Instructional Changes Without CBM Trendlines and Data-Based Decision Rules
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Apply CBM Aimlines, the 4-Point Decision Rule, and Diagnostic Error Analysis
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A progress-monitoring graph shows four consecutive weekly CBM data points falling below the aimline (or four above), or a teacher proposes waiting until the end of the grading period to adjust a failing reading intervention.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: What do the graphed CBM trendline and 4-point decision rule dictate right now, and which specific skill error in the probes should drive our Data-Based Individualization (DBI) change?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Read the CBM graph mechanics first (baseline median of 3 probes, aimline connecting baseline to annual goal, vertical phase-change lines, and consecutive points relative to the aimline) and spot distractors that rely on single-point noise or delay changes for months.
stages.requiredOutput: State whether the student's recent CBM points fall above, along, or below the aimline and flag any distractor that ignores the graphed trend.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Lock in Data-Based Individualization (DBI) and CBM decision rules: (1) administer brief, standardized, equivalent-difficulty probes on a consistent schedule (weekly/biweekly), (2) 4 consecutive data points BELOW the aimline → conduct diagnostic error analysis and intensify/adapt instruction (dosage, group size, explicitness, skill focus) while drawing a vertical phase-change line, (3) 4 consecutive data points ABOVE the aimline → raise the goal or fade intensity, and (4) never switch probes to easier grade levels arbitrarily without resetting the goal/trendline.
stages.requiredOutput: State the exact instructional action for 4 points below aimline, 4 points above aimline, and 1 single dip due to illness.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: A fourth grader's oral reading fluency CBM shows 4 straight weekly probes below the aimline; error analysis reveals 85% of errors occur on multisyllabic vowel-team and closed-syllable words rather than single-syllable CVC words. Decide the DBI adaptation.
stages.requiredOutput: Draw a vertical phase-change line, keep the CBM monitoring schedule intact, and shift intervention time from timed repeated reading to explicit multisyllabic decoding and syllable-division instruction.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Solve a fresh 5383 assessment item asking why Maze or Oral Reading Fluency (ORF) CBM probes are preferred over chapter unit tests for monitoring annual IEP reading goals.
stages.requiredOutput: Choose CBM's standardized equivalence across alternate forms, brevity, and high sensitivity to incremental skill growth over time.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Treating Dyslexia as a Visual Reversal Problem or Replacing Remediation with Accommodations Alone
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Target the Phonological Core of Dyslexia and Pair Access Accommodations with Remediation
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A case involves a student with dyslexia who reverses b/d or struggles to decode science textbooks in ninth grade, and distractors offer colored lenses/vision therapy or drop reading remediation entirely in favor of audiobooks alone.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does our plan directly remediate the phonological-orthographic language deficit through explicit structured literacy while using accommodations to protect grade-level content access without replacing instruction?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Spot two pervasive LD myths in distractors: (1) framing dyslexia as a visual/eye-tracking defect treatable by colored overlays or vision exercises, and (2) treating secondary accommodations (audiobooks, extended time) as a substitute for direct reading/writing remediation.
stages.requiredOutput: Flag the neurobiological myth or accommodation-only trap embedded in the distractor.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Ground remediation in the phonological-core deficit model of dyslexia: deliver explicit, systematic, cumulative, diagnostic structured literacy (phoneme-grapheme mapping, six syllable types, morphological analysis of Greek/Latin roots and affixes for older readers, fluency, and syntax) AND pair it with grade-level content access accommodations (text-to-speech, audio textbooks, graphic organizers, content-enhancement routines) so secondary students build both reading skill and background knowledge.
stages.requiredOutput: Explain why b/d reversals in early grades reflect fragile orthographic-phonological memory rather than backward vision, and design a dual-track plan (remediation + access) for a high schooler with dyslexia.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: A tenth grader with dyslexia has strong listening comprehension (85th percentile) but reads biology text at a fifth-grade decoding level. Evaluate two proposals: (A) give audiobooks only and remove reading goals, vs. (B) provide audio access in biology plus 30 minutes of explicit multisyllabic/morphological decoding and content-enhancement study strategies.
stages.requiredOutput: Justify why Proposal B delivers FAPE by preserving rigorous biology access while still closing the underlying decoding and morphological gap.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5383 characteristics vignette where a parent asks the IEP team to fund tinted overlays and eye-tracking software to cure their third grader's dyslexia.
stages.requiredOutput: Respond respectfully using peer-reviewed evidence: decline unproven visual-training therapies via informed collaboration and direct IEP resources toward explicit phonological-orthographic structured literacy.
